views.label: A · close to current tone, reduced footprint
views.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: a single portrait photorealistic rug comparison in this actual reception room.
Input image 1 is EDIT TARGET, Reception Room 01's doorway view. Keep EXACT camera, crop, perspective, room size, furniture positions, lighting, paint and all decor. Change ONLY the rug.
User likes the current large traditional brown rug, but wants it a little smaller so it does not meet the BLACK GRID / STEEL GLAZED DOOR SCREEN. Leave a modest, deliberate exposed OAK FLOOR STRIP between rug and black steel doorway/threshold, around 20-25cm visually (about one floorboard width), NOT a huge moat of bare floor.
RUG FIT: keep a substantial rectangle anchoring BOTH green chairs and the little walnut table. Pull the near/entrance end of rug back towards fireplace by roughly 20-25cm. If required also trim its edge beside the left black door frame slightly so a narrow continuous strip of oak is clearly visible there, rather than the rug touching the fixed steel frame. Keep rug front edge visible; do not crop it off. Rug should look only modestly smaller, not a small mat floating beneath the table. Keep original orientation parallel to fireplace wall, not diagonal. Retain both armchair FRONT feet on the rug and keep office chair caster area on oak. Do not move furniture, doors or camera to fake the gap. Preserve and restore the original oak planks/grain where rug is removed. No new threshold, frame or floor pattern. The gap is from the fixed doorway/threshold line, not the end of the swung-open glass leaf.
LOCK EVERYTHING ELSE: actual original green bentwood chairs and cushions, small walnut pedestal table with one dish, mantel/print/shelf books and decor, rug-independent hearth clearance, reading lamp, bay desk TWO monitors and task chair, pedestal at desk right, task lamp right, piano/bench, sheer and linen curtains, original taupe walls, white mouldings and ceiling/chandelier, floor and black steel glazed doors, all photographic detail. No painting, extra objects, rearranged shelves, new chairs or new room.
Material is real matte low-pile wool with softly aged Persian-style floral pattern, similar character and scale to input, not bright geometric, sisal or modern abstract. In-focus textile and original room, no Gaussian blur. No captions, labels, text or watermark.
OPTION A: retain the current rug's warm tobacco/stone-brown colour, subdued moss/ochre touches and gently aged traditional floral drawing almost exactly. This is the comparison baseline showing the improved smaller footprint and visible doorway gap. Do not make it lighter or darker. Keep subtle border, avoid adding high-contrast outlines.
